utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-81-A, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I wanted to make sure that the audio equipment is working properly. Everybody can hear me. Yes. Mr. Perisic, can you hear me in a language you can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances of the parties. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. CROSS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Appearing for the Prosecution, I'm Matthew Cross, together with Ms. Helen Brady, and our Case Manager is Colin Nawrot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cross. For Mr. Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Gregor Guy-Smith and Holly Buchanan, appearing on behalf of Mr. Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. As you are all aware, Rule 65 ter (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the filing of a Notice of Appeal and, thereafter, within 120 days after the last Status Conference of for each Appellant in the Tribunal's custody. A Status Conference serves two primary purposes. First, it allows the Appellant an opportunity to express concerns relating to his appeal or detention conditions. Second, it provides an opportunity to update the Appellant with respect to the status of his case. The Status Conference is also an opportunity for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained person. In the present case, the Notice of Appeal was filed on 8 November 2011. Today's Status Conference was scheduled by an order issued on 6 February 2012. So let me now turn to inquiring into Mr. Perisic's health. If Mr. Perisic wishes it, I can close the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I understand that there is no need from Mr. Perisic's perspective. So I would like to ask the parties whether they have any other issues which they would like to raise at this time. Any issues for the Prosecution, Mr. Cross?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: None on behalf of Mr. Perisic at this time, Your Honour. But thank you for asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Since there are no matters to be raised, I thank the parties for their attendance and call the proceedings to a close. Thank you very much.
